# Perks still to wire

A perk is wired when it carries an `effects` block typed against
`resources/data/perk_effects.json`. A perk leaves this document when it does,
so the counts are the progress bar.

**8 of 603 perks are typed.** 138 more have a
hand-written `has_perk` check somewhere in the combat code — those work, but each
one is a bespoke `if` statement rather than data, which is why the other four
hundred were never done.

## The thing to understand first

Perks cannot be migrated from their descriptions automatically, and the reason is
worth stating plainly: **almost none of them are unconditional.** Of 603 perks,
about 19 are a plain standing bonus. Everything else fires while wielding
something, against a certain kind of target, on a trigger, or on a particular
school of spell. The condition is not a detail attached to the effect — it *is*
most of the content.

So the work is not 597 individual migrations. It is implementing conditions, in
order of how many perks each unlocks. Implement `wielding` and every perk in that
section below becomes a data edit rather than a code change.

Both classifications are a reading of the prose by regex, not something the data
asserts. They are right often enough to size the job and group it; they will be
wrong on individual perks, and the per-perk entries below print the description
so the call can be made from the text.
